scope: Source-only novelty adjudication of reopened-pass candidates A and B; original standard base/core and applicable FAQ only. No summary, reader, grades, or reviewer reports were read for this adjudication.
policy_applied: Credit a newly requested rule, defined outcome branch, or consequential timing/exception interaction. Do not credit cosmetic variants or pure recombinations. Read actual question parts, without treating extra key explanation as asked coverage.

decisions.title: Dahan-only protection leaves land Damage and Blight intact and does not stop counterattack
decisions.reason: The original Concealing Shadows face supplies a recipient-specific Damage prevention instruction missing from the actual existing prompts. Its protection applies only to Dahan Damage from Ravaging Invaders. That creates a distinct Ravage outcome: the land still takes its ordinary Damage and may Blight, Dahan remain unharmed, and surviving Dahan counterattack because the Ravage occurred. This is a new core-card exception governing one recipient; it is not merely different Ravage arithmetic.

comparisons_to_actual_questions.Q06: Unprotected Ravage, so land and Dahan take the same ordinary Damage. It does not test recipient-specific prevention.
comparisons_to_actual_questions.Q07: Tests Defend reducing overall Invader Damage to zero versus skipping Ravage. Neither asks about leaving land Damage intact while preventing only Dahan Damage.
comparisons_to_actual_questions.Q31: Tests additive Defend and full-strength damaged pieces. Defend reduces both Damage recipients, unlike Concealing Shadows.
comparisons_to_actual_questions.Q65: Asks whether Infinite Vitality protects against Remove/Replace and whether its Blight protection prevents choosing a cascade destination. It never asks to resolve a Ravage with Dahan-only Damage prevention. Its extra key text cannot substitute for that missing requested branch.
comparisons_to_actual_questions.Q101: Tests retaining an existing Sacred Site Defend through simultaneous land/Dahan Damage and resulting site loss. The prevention still applies to both recipients; it does not test this asymmetry.

decisions.question: Concealing Shadows has resolved on a land with one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan. The land has no Blight and no Defend. Resolve its Ravage: what Damage reaches the land and Dahan, is Blight added, and do the Dahan counterattack? Assume any Presence loss does not end the game.
decisions.predetermined_answer: Invaders still deal 3 Damage to the land, adding one Blight and resolving its normal Presence consequences. The Dahan take no Damage from those Ravaging Invaders, so both survive unharmed. Concealing Shadows neither reduces land Damage nor skips Ravage. The two Dahan counterattack for 4 total Damage to Invaders, allocated normally.

source_refs.label: Original base Unique Power face, Concealing Shadows
source_refs.verified_symbols_and_text: Fast; Range 0; target ANY; 1 Fear; Dahan symbol followed by take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn. No expansion set mark. The Fear instruction is a separate already-resolved Power effect, not Ravage Damage prevention.
source_refs.set_membership_basis: Parent-provided original-base Unique identity, corroborated by supplied face and absent expansion mark; no inference from broad FAQ category membership.

decisions.title: Explicit Fear plus destruction Fear, with an impossible Destroy instruction
decisions.predetermined_answer_if_asked: With one actual Town destroyed, generate 2 total Fear: 1 explicit Fear plus 1 automatic destruction Fear. If the Destroy instruction cannot be performed on an otherwise legal target, generate the explicit 1 Fear and skip only the impossible Destroy instruction.
decisions.reason: Both requested outcomes are mechanical recombinations of procedures already requested. Q18 asks how Destroy differs from Damage/Remove/Replace for Fear and survival, which directly requires the automatic Fear consequence of actual destruction. Q11 expressly asks resolution of Fear generated by an effect. Adding these independently generated amounts requires no new timing rule, modifier, replacement, or exception. The no-Town branch directly instantiates Q16: retain the feasible printed Fear instruction and skip the impossible Destroy instruction on a legal target. Neither operation is conditional on the other unless a card says so.
decisions.strict_actual_prompt_distinction: This rejection does not credit Q18 with literally asking the words in addition to explicit Fear, and does not rely on the key adding that explanation. Q18 establishes the destruction-Fear procedure; Q11 establishes explicit effect Fear; Q16 establishes what happens to another feasible instruction when one instruction is impossible. The proposed question merely runs those already-tested procedures together.
decisions.faq_assessment: FAQ .7w4g8pr confirms that both Fear sources apply and supplies Shatter Homesteads as an original-core example. A dedicated FAQ clarification establishes the correct answer, but it does not itself establish novelty when the candidate adds only the composition of already-tested independent instructions and their arithmetic.
